title: USCIS Updates Policy Guidance for the “Sought to Acquire” Requirement Under the Child Status Protection Act
paragraphs: We are updating theUSCIS Policy Manualto clarify how we will apply the extraordinary circumstances exception to the “sought to acquire” requirement under the Child Status Protection Act (CSPA) in light of a Feb. 14, 2023, policy change. Thisupdate  (PDF, 331.87 KB):

The CSPA protects certain beneficiaries from losing their eligibility for immigrant visas and adjustment of status because they age during the immigration process and no longer qualify as a child for immigration purposes. To benefit from the CSPA, aliens must seek to acquire lawful permanent resident status within 1 year of when an immigrant visa becomes available. On Feb. 14 USCIS issued policy guidance updating when an immigrant visa becomes available for the purpose of calculating an applicant’s CSPA age.

Under the policy guidance in effect before Feb. 14, 2023, some aliens may not have applied to adjust their status because a visa was not available to calculate CSPA age under the prior policy or the alien’s CSPA age would have been calculated to be over 21 years old. If these aliens apply to adjust their status under the new policy issued on Feb. 14, they may not be able to meet the 1-year sought to acquire requirement. However, aliens who do not meet this requirement may still benefit from the CSPA if they can establish that their failure to meet the requirement was the result of extraordinary circumstances.
Visit thePolicy Manual Feedbackpage to comment on this update. USCIS welcomes feedback on this guidance and will consider any comments received in future updates.
